initial.prompt:
<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>
This puzzle replaces every non-zero cell with color 5; zero cells stay 0.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>

5 0 5
0 5 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<example_3>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

% ---------- Grid dimensions ----------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% ---------- Row and column ranges ----------
row(R) :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- C >= 0, C < M.

% ---------- Bounding box of non‑zero cells ----------
r_min(Rmin) :- Rmin = #min{R : input(R, _, _)}.
r_max(Rmax) :- Rmax = #max{R : input(R, _, _)}.
c_min(Cmin) :- Cmin = #min{C : input(_, C, _)}.
c_max(Cmax) :- Cmax = #max{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% ---------- Shape dimensions ----------
shape_h(H) :- H = Rmax - Rmin + 1.
shape_w(W)  :- W = Cmax - Cmin + 1.

% ---------- Rotated coordinates of every input cell ----------
rot(Rin, Cin, Rrot, Crot) :-
    r_min(Rmin), r_max(Rmax), c_min(Cmin), c_max(Cmax),
    Rin >= Rmin, Rin <= Rmax, Cin >= Cmin, Cin <= Cmax,
    Rrot = Cin - Cmin,
    Crot = W - 1 - (Rin - Rmin).

% ---------- Rotated shape cells together with their colour ----------
rotated(Rin, Cin, Rrot, Crot, Color) :-
    rot(Rin, Cin, Rrot, Crot), input(Rin, Cin, Color).

% ---------- Gravity offset ----------
int(O).
O >= 0.
O < N.

% Conflict at a given offset O
conflict(O) :-
    O >= 0, O < N,
    1 { rot(Rrot, Crot) : (Rrot+O >= N) } 1 :- true.
conflict(O) :-
    O >= 0, O < N,
    1 { rot(Rrot, Crot) : input(Rrot+O, Crot, _) } 1 :- true.

% O must be a valid offset (no conflict at O)
:- not conflict(O).

% Maximal offset: there must be a conflict at O+1 (unless O = N‑1)
1 { out_term(Rrot, Crot) : (Rrot+O+1 >= N), overlap_term(Rrot, Crot) : input(Rrot+O+1, Crot, _) } 1 :- true.

% ---------- Shape cells after gravity ----------
shape_cell(Rout, Cout) :-
    rotated(Rin, Cin, Rrot, Crot, Color),
    O,
    Rout = Rrot + O,
    Cout = Crot.

% ---------- Output for the rotated part (coloured as in the input) ----------
output(Rout, Cout, Color) :-
    rotated(Rin, Cin, Rrot, Crot, Color),
    O,
    Rout = Rrot + O,
    Cout = Crot,
    Rout >= 0, Rout < N,
    Cout >= 0, Cout < M,
    not input(Rout, Cout, _).

% ---------- Output for all other cells (stay zero) ----------
output(R, C, 0) :-
    output_cell(R, C),
    not shape_cell(R, C).

% ---------- Exactly one colour per output cell ----------
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

row(R) :- n_rows(N), R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C >= 0, C < M.

% Non-zero cells
nonzero(R,C) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0.

% Cells with at least one non-zero neighbor (large component)
has_nonzero_neighbor(R,C) :-
    (R > 0, input(R-1, C, Color2), Color2 != 0) ;
    (R < N-1, input(R+1, C, Color2), Color2 != 0) ;
    (C > 0, input(R, C-1, Color2), Color2 != 0) ;
    (C < M-1, input(R, C+1, Color2), Color2 != 0).

large_cell(R,C) :- nonzero(R,C), has_nonzero_neighbor(R,C).

% Rotated component raw (clockwise rotation)
rotated_raw(Rrot, Crot, Color, OrigR, Cin, RotR) :-
    large_cell(R,C), Color = input(R,C,Color),
    Rrot = M - 1 - C,
    Crot = R,
    OrigR = R,
    Cin = C,
    RotR = M - 1 - C.

% Gravity: compute offset (how many rotated cells are below this one)
gravity_offset(Rrot, Crot, Color, OrigR, Cin, RotR, Offset, Rout) :-
    rotated_raw(Rrot, Crot, Color, OrigR, Cin, RotR),
    #count{R2 : rotated_raw(R2, Crot, _, _, _, OrigR2), OrigR2 > OrigR} = Offset,
    Rout = RotR + Offset,
    Rout >= 0,

% Rotated component final placement (only on originally empty cells)

    gravity_offset(Rrot, Crot, Color, OrigR, Cin, RotR, Offset, Rout),
    not input(Rout, Crot, _).

% Original component unchanged

% Candidate colors for each cell

candidate(R,C,0) :- not original_comp(R,C,_), not rotated_comp(R,C,_).

% Output cell definition
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

output(R,C,Color) :- candidate(R,C,Color).

% Exactly one color per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

col(C) :- C >= 0, C < M.

col(C) :- C >= 0, C < M.
